title: Given strings s1, s2, and s3, determine whether s3 is formed by interleaving s1 and s2, preserving the left-to-right order of each.
shortTitle: Interleaving String — can two strings interleave to form a third

s1_definition.profdef: 2D DP where dp[i][j] is true if the first i characters of s1 and first j of s2 can interleave to form the first i+j characters of s3. dp[i][j] holds if the last char came from s1 (dp[i−1][j] and s1[i−1]==s3[i+j−1]) or from s2 (dp[i][j−1] and s2[j−1]==s3[i+j−1]). Time O(m·n), space O(n).
s1_definition.analogy: A merge auditor at National Bank of India checks whether a combined transaction stream was produced by interleaving two source streams without reordering either. At each merged position she asks whether the next character could have come from stream one or from stream two, keeping each stream's internal order.
s1_definition.oneliner: dp[i][j] = (fromS1 and match) OR (fromS2 and match); length must equal m+n.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** 2D DP where dp[i][j] is true if the first i characters of s1 and first j of s2 can interleave to form the first i+j characters of s3. dp[i][j] holds if the last char came from s1 (dp[i−1][j] and s1[i−1]==s3[i+j−1]) or from s2 (dp[i][j−1] and s2[j−1]==s3[i+j−1]). Time O(m·n), space O(n).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A merge auditor at National Bank of India checks whether a combined transaction stream was produced by interleaving two source streams without reordering either. At each merged position she asks whether the next character could have come from stream one or from stream two, keeping each stream's internal order.

**One line to remember:** dp[i][j] = (fromS1 and match) OR (fromS2 and match); length must equal m+n.

sections.s2_technical:
First, if the length of s3 is not the sum of the lengths of s1 and s2, return false immediately. Otherwise build a boolean table dp of size (m+1) by (n+1), where dp[i][j] says whether the first i of s1 and first j of s2 can interleave into the first i+j of s3. The base case dp[0][0] is true.

Each merged character at position i+j−1 of s3 must come from either s1 or s2. It came from s1 if dp[i−1][j] is true and s1 at i−1 equals s3 at i+j−1; it came from s2 if dp[i][j−1] is true and s2 at j−1 equals s3 at i+j−1. For example: `dp[i][j] = (i>0 && dp[i-1][j] && s1.charAt(i-1)==s3.charAt(i+j-1)) || (j>0 && dp[i][j-1] && s2.charAt(j-1)==s3.charAt(i+j-1));`. The answer is dp[m][n].

The time is O(m·n) and space reduces to O(n) with a rolling row. A senior nuance is that a naive recursive interleaving check branches exponentially, so the whole point of the DP is to collapse the overlapping subproblems defined purely by the pair of prefix lengths.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, a merge auditor verifies that a combined event stream was produced by interleaving two source feeds without reordering either feed. This is exactly how Interleaving String works.

Problem 2 — A greedy character-by-character match fails because at a position both feeds may offer the same next character and only one choice leads to a full valid interleave. This is exactly why the DP explores both origins at every cell.

The mini-project builds a `StreamMergeAuditor`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The inputs are aabcc, dbbca, and the candidate aadbbcbcac.

Step 1: The lengths five and five sum to ten, which matches the candidate length, so the check proceeds.

Step 2: dp of zero and zero is true, the empty interleaving.

Step 3: Each cell is set true if the current merged character could come from s1 with a true left-neighbor-up, or from s2 with a true neighbor to the left.

Step 4: The true states propagate through the grid following valid character matches from either source.

Step 5: The bottom-right cell is true so the first candidate is a valid interleaving, while the second candidate blocks somewhere and ends false.

```text
2026-10-27T04:10:00Z [INFO] aabcc + dbbca = aadbbcbcac → true
2026-10-27T04:10:00Z [INFO] isInterleave = false
2026-10-27T04:10:00Z [INFO] aabcc + dbbca = aadbbbaccc → false
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```text
  s1=aabcc  s2=dbbca  s3=aadbbcbcac  (len 5+5=10)
  dp[0][0]=true
  dp[i][j] = (dp[i-1][j] && s1[i-1]==s3[i+j-1])     ← char from s1
          || (dp[i][j-1] && s2[j-1]==s3[i+j-1])     ← char from s2
  dp[5][5] = true → valid interleaving
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Interleaving String is a two-dimensional dynamic programming problem. First I do a quick guard: if the length of the third string is not the sum of the lengths of the first two, it cannot be an interleaving, so I return false immediately. Otherwise I define dp of i and j as whether the first i characters of the first string and the first j of the second can interleave to form the first i plus j characters of the third.

For each cell the current merged character must have come from exactly one of the two sources. It came from the first string if the cell above was reachable and the first string's character matches, or it came from the second string if the cell to the left was reachable and the second string's character matches. The base case is the empty-empty cell being true, and the answer is the bottom-right cell.

In my project at National Bank of India, a merge auditor verified that a combined event stream was produced by interleaving two source feeds without reordering either. A greedy match fails when both feeds offer the same next character and only one choice completes a valid interleave, so I used this DP keyed on the pair of prefix lengths, which collapses the exponential recursion into a quadratic table.
